newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish higher, near highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish higher, near highs.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended higher for a second straight day, first aided by U.S. data and then by technical momentum.
Traders tied the morning's strength to followthrough from a firm close Wednesday and to a lack of bearish surprises in early U.S. data.
They said July consumer prices and industrial output and capacity use data continued to show an economy with moderate growth and low inflation.
Intraday technicals aided gains, and short-covering nudged most contracts to close near session highs.
But while the short-term looks more friendly, Hare said ample resistance rests above the market.
A T-bond futures trader agreed, saying September T-bonds needed to close above 114-12/32 before the mood would turn more bullish intermediate-term.
Traders noted that firms were active on both sides of the market, though overall activity was more subdued than it has been the previous two days.
One trader said a strong dollar aided the debt futures tone.

Technical strength gained momentum earlier in the day when September Treasury bonds crept above 113-16/32, traders said. Light buystops were triggered there to take September above Wednesday's 113-19/32 high, traders said.
The upmove turns the short-term technical picture slightly positive, said Paul Hare, technican with LIT's The Linn Group.
He said recent losses nearly completed a 50-percent retracement of the 105-30/32 to 116-31/32 rally, and this week's action sets the market up for gains into mid-114-00.
"It looks like 112-00 is going to hold this move and we should probably go to 114-16/32," Hare said.

U.S. July consumer prices rose 0.2 percent both overall and excluding food and energy, in line with forecasts. Later, July industrial output was reported up 0.2 percent, compared with a revised 0.3-percent gain in June. Capacity use was 83.1 percent versus 83.3 in June and a forecast for 83.5 percent.

At the close, September T-bonds rose 25/32 to 113-20/32, 10-year notes gained 14/32 to 109-11/32, muni-bonds gained 23/32 to 119-25/32, December Eurodollars rallied 0.035 to 94.095, and T-bills added 0.035 at 94.795. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
